full_text: Progress Notes Signed Jul 29, 2026. Progress Notes by Paul Johnson at 7/29/2026 11:26 AM. BARTZ-ALTADONNA COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTER, 43322 Gingham Avenue, Lancaster, CA, 93535. CHIEF COMPLAINT: Nicolas presents for Complete Physical Exam (Pt presents to Establish care/ Physical./Pt presents with c/o being previously prescribed diazepam and last taken on 7/8. Pt reports he went into AVMC on 7/13, 7/14 and 7/15 due to withdrawal symptoms. Pt reports his anxiety is worse after his last dose of diazepam). SUBJECTIVE: Nicolas Hernandez presents to the clinic today to establish care, agrees to labs with telephone follow up. Numerous ED visits re benzodiazepine withdrawal. He was working with a psychiatric provider and receiving benzodiazepines and suboxone for his anxiety and fentanyl abuse. Used fentanyl x 4-5 years. Off fentanyl since August last year. I declined to provide benzodiazepines to the patient, he has withdrawn several times, We discussed this and I discourage this, We discussed brain receptors, what substances appeal and why. Per him he is on several strengths of suboxone, will let addiction medicine manage this as well. Will refer to Addiction medicine for management. Follow up in two weeks by phone re lab results. Currently not working, has living space, has food. Past Medical History: Substance abuse (CMS & HHS-HCC). Social History: Alcohol use: Never. Drug use: Never. Psychiatric/Behavioral: Positive for sleep disturbance. The patient is nervous/anxious. Vitals: BP: 102/69, Pulse: (!) 108 (Tachycardia), Temp: 97.5 F, SpO2: 96%, Weight: 111 lb 9.6 oz (50.6 kg), Height: 5' 6". BMI: 18.01 (Underweight). Allergies: Tramadol (Pt reports seizures occur). Visit Diagnoses: Well adult exam - Primary (ICD-10-CM: Z00.00), History of substance abuse (Chronic) (ICD-10-CM: F19.11), Anxiety (ICD-10-CM: F41.9). Relevant Orders: REFERRAL TO ADDICTION MEDICINE.
summary: Official MyChart Progress Notes for Nicolas Hernandez at Bartz-Altadonna Community Health Center, signed by Dr. Paul Johnson (DO) on July 29, 2026. The notes document the clinician's refusal to provide a safe benzodiazepine tapering or bridging protocol despite noting the patient's active tachycardia (pulse 108 bpm), anxiety, and history of forced street-sourcing and multiple emergency room visits for withdrawal.
